body: Owner grade: RED executed RED-FT-08 as FIRED (committed b79c04c9a). REALIZED is therefore foreclosed for the November 10 resolution, so -001's line that the composition test 'still needs November 10' is now incomplete. title: Russian diesel: the first post-deal cargo loaded October 13 (one ~40,000 t tanker, Primorsk to Morocco); Novak's 3.5 Mt/month is a conditional target that contradicts his own path; a US export ban is dormant
origin: Reuters October 14 (LSEG shipping data) via Baird Maritime
confidence_language: cargo confirmed (one source chain); targets are statements
dispatch_note: Research-intake BRENT watch hits (6) verified by a read-only RULE 9 helper. Follows SIG-W-20261010-003 (GL-135) and SIG-W-20261013-004 (Senate rescission letter); same action lines as -1010-003 minus OSPREY (no strike content). The untraceable 'Middle East diesel exports -52%' figure is killed in kill_log, not routed.
body: Physical: Reuters, using LSEG shipping data (October 14), reports one tanker with about 40,000 t of ultra-low-sulphur diesel loaded at Primorsk on October 13, bound for Morocco, after Russia partially lifted its diesel export ban from October 10 under the US agreement (OFAC GL-135, SIG-W-20261010-003). It is one cargo, not a flow rate: about 13% of Novak's own 300 kt October figure. Statements: Deputy PM Novak (TASS, Russian Energy Week, October 14) said Russia 'could' raise diesel exports to 3.5 Mt/month by year-end and take 10% of the market, that supply contracts are being examined with US counterparts 'at the level of ministries and companies', and (Moscow Times) that supplies will go 'to the U.S. directly'. Caveats that travel: a conditional, self-interested target, not loadings data; it contradicts his own October 9-10 path (300 kt October, 500 kt November, 1 Mt December), so 3-3.5 Mt by year-end needs roughly a threefold jump; the '10%' basis is ambiguous (future share per Moscow Times, previously held share per Oilprice). Benchmarks: under 1 Mt in June 2026 versus about 2.5 Mt/month a year earlier (trader estimates via Reuters/Oilprice). US export ban: a Mexico Business News piece on the threat to Mexico (October 14, not retrievable) has no new measure behind it. The last live actions were Sep 17 bills (H.R. 10423), September 22 Trump support, an October 2 Trump 'no ban', and October 8, when the Senate GOP effort collapsed. The idea could revive on a diesel spike. Mexico exposure figures use different bases; do not merge them: about 220 kb/d of US distillate exports (Argus citing EIA); 'roughly 60%' of Mexico's diesel (CRS); 40% of fuel supply (MBN headline). Product-market context with its basis: the IEA (October 14) puts Middle East plus Russia combined net gasoil exports at 820 kb/d in September, down 1.3 mb/d, more than 60% y/y.
sources: [The National on the IEA OMR, October 14](https://www.thenationalnews.com/business/energy/2026/10/14/diesel-shortage-to-persist-into-2027-as-iran-war-disrupts-supply-iea-warns/)
ask: BRENT: integrate the first physical cargo (one 40 kt loading) into the diesel-supply work; do not convert Novak's target into a flow. YURI: log Novak's conditional target and the 'contracts with US ministries' statement as state-actor intent, with the internal-path contradiction attached.

why.HANS: EU diesel supply and the allied reaction.

title: GFS Pride: cause still unresolved, the IRGC mine claim named no ship, and the IMO counts it as the war's second loss, not a 'first mine sinking'; Cape Dao reportedly sinking; Houthi source tells Aramco shareholders to sell
origin: AFP/Aaj relay of IRGC Navy statement via Tasnim/Mehr/Fars
confidence_language: claims confirmed as claims; cause and Cape Dao unconfirmed
dispatch_note: Will bookmarks (HormuzLetter 'first vessel sunk by a mine'; MenchOsint AIS-off; FirstSquawk Tasnim Aramco line) verified by a read-only RULE 9 helper. Iran pre-dispatch guard consulted: IRAN_WAR_GUARDS Tasnim-mine-claim block (claim must not fire GATE 2 on relay), VESSEL-SUNK theater check, ADD#26. Anchor full sweep last 2026-10-08; the MPA-confirmed GFS Pride sinking is a ladder re-verify trigger and the calendar sweep is due 2026-10-15. FALCON owns census/gate eligibility.
body: 1) GFS PRIDE (follows SIG-W-20261014-002). Cause is unresolved. Singapore's MPA says 'unidentified projectile', and Reuters maritime-security sources also say projectile. The mine claim came from the IRGC Navy public-relations office, no individual named, via Tasnim, Mehr and Fars on the morning of October 14. It described a container ship on an 'unauthorised and dangerous' route that 'struck a mine that exploded' and sank, carrying more than 2,500 containers and 'contraband', but it did not name the ship; Maritime Executive identifies GFS PRIDE from the IRGC images (2,824 TEU, 39,446 dwt, built 2008). Marisks (via CNBC): 'no independent evidence' a mine caused it. No CENTCOM statement on the ship was found, the owner was unreachable, and there is no UAE statement. UKMTO reported two unnamed container ships (about 50,000 t and 19,000 t) with 'minor damage' around 16:40-17:00 GMT October 13, which does not cleanly match a vessel that sank. The circulating 'first vessel sunk by a mine in the war' appears in none of the primary texts; the IMO counts GFS PRIDE as the SECOND vessel lost since February 28 (the first being Safeen Prestige, per gCaptain). Do not count a mine detonation on this claim. The '10 days AIS off' claim is unverified. New: the bulk carrier Cape Dao (Antigua and Barbuda flag, UAE-managed; struck September 23 about 15 nm NE of Khasab, one seafarer killed) is reportedly sinking after a failed salvage (Vanguard, single source). That would be a further loss if confirmed; FALCON adjudicates against its owner count. 2) Aramco threat. An unnamed 'military source' quoted by the Houthi-run Saba agency (YPA, October 14) said: 'We advise Aramco shareholders to dispose of their shares so they do not incur losses in the coming days.' It is not attributed to Yahya Saree; 'hand over' and 'heavy losses' in the circulating version are not in the text. It is a threat statement naming no target or date. Context: the Saudi Energy Ministry said an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran was 'targeted, resulting in a limited fire' late October 13, with no casualties, while Reuters company sources describe a ballistic-missile hit on an HQ office tower with 'extensive damage' and operations continuing; that tension is unresolved (SIG-W-20261013-008, -1014-002).
sources: gCaptain and WorldCargo News October 14 (read by helper)
AFP via Aaj relay of the IRGC Navy statement (Tasnim/Mehr/Fars)
ask: FALCON: reconcile GFS PRIDE's cause (claim vs projectile) and the IMO 'second loss' count with your owner census, and check the Cape Dao report before any count moves. BRENT: carry the Aramco threat as a statement only; no output loss is established.

title: UN official warns a food crisis in parts of Asia and Africa could follow if the US and Iran do not agree on the Hormuz fertilizer plan within weeks; no fertilizer deal 'failed'
dispatch_note: Will bookmark (Polymarket: 'UN warns of a major food crisis ... as the U.S. & Iran fail to reach a deal'). RULE 9 helper verdict CORRECTED-FRAMING: a conditional forward warning, not a failed negotiation. Nitrogen (urea) and sulphur at full FERT depth; not potash. RED on info per CORRECTED-FRAMING.
body: Jorge Moreira da Silva, UN Under-Secretary-General and head of UNOPS, who oversees the UN Hormuz fertilizer taskforce (not FAO or WFP), told Reuters in Bangkok on October 14 that failure by the US and Iran to agree on the UN plan within weeks COULD trigger a food-security crisis in parts of Asia and Africa: 'It's absolutely crucial to get the deal in the next few weeks. Otherwise, we will miss the planting season.' The mechanism was drafted after the taskforce formed in March but is not activated. It could start 7-10 days after a US-Iran agreement: an Oman coordination centre would register vessels, UN monitors would verify loading at Gulf ports and ships would be tracked, moving about five ships a day. There was no discrete fertilizer negotiation that failed; broader indirect US-Iran exchanges have stalled since the June interim arrangement collapsed. The White House, State Department and Iran's embassy did not comment. Figures with basis: before the war Hormuz carried about one-third of globally traded urea and nearly half of seaborne sulphur (Reuters); IFPRI says Gulf fertilizer exports remain 'largely' halted; an ICC August scenario put cereals up to +81% and oil crops +66% if the disruption continues (a scenario, not a forecast). The circulating tweet turned a forward conditional into an accomplished failure.
ask: FERT: integrate the dated UN conditional (planting-season window, 7-10 day activation lag, five ships a day) into the nitrogen/sulphur supply read; no price or tender change is reported.

title: Zelensky says Ukraine was 'betrayed', tied mainly to the Russian diesel deal; Starlink speed cap partly eased; Musk says limits are decided by the US military and 'ultimately POTUS'; no US government confirmation
origin: Piers Morgan Uncensored, aired October 14 (via AOL/Mirror)
confidence_language: quotes confirmed; cause of the cap unestablished
dispatch_note: Will bookmark (unusual_whales: Zelensky betrayed; Starlink blocked; 'people were killed'). RULE 9 helper: quotes confirmed, 'people were killed' CORRECTED to a forecast, no US government confirmation. Follows SIG-W-20261014-009 (same action line). RED on info per CORRECTED-FRAMING.
body: Follows SIG-W-20261014-009 (moving-terminal restriction). Zelensky answered 'Yes' on Piers Morgan (aired October 14) when asked whether the Trump administration had betrayed Ukraine; CNN ties this mainly to the Russian diesel deal (SIG-W-20261010-003, -024), which he called a 'simple victory' for the Kremlin. On Starlink he said 'I am sure they knew what they did' and that it 'was blocked by SpaceX and the United States', but the same day in London (AFP) he said 'I hope that it's a mistake, maybe huge technical problem' and 'We count on (our) partnership with the United States'. Correction to the circulating post: he did not report deaths; he said 'this decision will bring a lot of human losses... people will die' (a forecast). Musk on X, verbatim: 'Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government'; 'Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS'; Starlink is commercial and SpaceX-controlled. There is no US government confirmation of who ordered the cap: Axios (via Mirror) quotes two White House officials that Ukraine contacted the Pentagon, which 'controls Starshield', and that Trump was reportedly reaching out to SpaceX. Mechanism: a 100 mph (160 km/h) speed cap on moving terminals imposed overnight October 13-14 without notice disrupted drone missions; on October 14 Fedorov said speeds up to 160 km/h are being restored, while the Defence Ministry says the cap remains. Context: on October 10 Trump said 'time for Ukraine to get a new president' and Musk said 'Zelensky has gone too far' (Newsweek). Not established: who ordered the cap; Ukrainian claims of US direction are unevidenced. A 'not a high-level policy decision' snippet in search results could not be found in any fetched text and is not carried.
sources: Newsweek and Meduza on Musk's X post (read by helper)
ask: OSPREY: update the Starshield restriction read with the partial easing (cap still in place per the Defence Ministry) and the political rift; who ordered the cap remains unestablished.
